name: Tailoring and alteration shops

problems.words: Before Eid we take more orders than we can stitch
quick_ideas: Work out how many pieces your team really finishes in a week, so you know your limit
Stop taking bookings once that limit is reached, since a late suit costs more goodwill than a polite no.

workzap_build.text: a capacity planner that warns you when booked orders exceed what the team can make.

problems.ask_first: How many karigars work for you?
problems.free_stops: Capacity rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, count how many promised pieces are still unfinished each evening, so you see your real Eid backlog before accepting more.
Give one person the job of writing every promised delivery date in one notebook, so new bookings match what the team can finish.

problems.words: Customers come on the promised date and the suit isn't ready
quick_ideas: List every order due this week with its stage, so late ones show early
Tell customers about delays before they arrive, since a warning upsets them less than an empty hanger.

workzap_build.text: an order status board with "ready" or delay messages sent to customers.

problems.ask_first: How do you record orders now?
problems.free_stops: Status flow stays for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Each morning, count how many orders due this week are still at cutting, stitching or finishing, so delays show before collection day.
Give one person the job of checking tomorrow's promised orders before closing, so missing work is chased while there is still time.

problems.words: We lose slips and can't find the fabric
quick_ideas: Number every order and tag the fabric with the same number, so the two never separate
Keep a copy of each slip, so a lost slip isn't a lost order.

workzap_build.text: a digital order slip with a copy sent to the customer on WhatsApp.

problems.ask_first: Do customers bring their own fabric?
problems.free_stops: Slip setup is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, note each time a slip or fabric bundle takes extra time to find, so you see where orders get separated.
Keep all new order slips in one counter folder until handover to the workshop, so fabric and paperwork travel together.

problems.words: Wrong measurements and the suit has to be redone
quick_ideas: Note every rework and its reason, so patterns show
See which step causes most, since that is where to fix.

workzap_build.text: a rework log with reasons to spot patterns.

problems.free_stops: Log setup stays for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, mark each redone suit by reason in a notebook, so you see whether errors start at measuring, cutting or stitching.
Give one person the job of checking the slip against the garment before handover, so avoidable rework is caught before fitting.

problems.words: Piece-rate payments are calculated by hand and disputed
quick_ideas: Record pieces assigned and finished per karigar daily, so payday isn't rebuilt from memory
Share totals weekly, so disputes come up early.

workzap_build.text: a piece-rate log with weekly payout calculation.

problems.ask_first: How often do you pay karigars?
problems.free_stops: Payout rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one pay cycle, compare each karigar's finished pieces with what was assigned daily, so disputed totals are easier to trace.
Keep one notebook for pieces given out and returned, with one person updating it daily, so payday totals come from one record.

problems.words: Buttons, linings and threads run out at the worst time
quick_ideas: List the accessories you use most, so you know what matters
Stock up before Eid, since suppliers run short too.

workzap_build.text: an accessory and fabric tracker with reorder alerts.

problems.free_stops: Reorder levels stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, note every time work pauses for missing buttons, lining or thread, so you see which shortage interrupts stitching most.
Give one person the job of checking the accessories shelf before closing and writing shortages in one place, so replenishment gets noticed earlier.

problems.words: Advance taken but customer never comes back
quick_ideas: List all uncollected orders, so you know what's sitting there
Contact each customer once, since many simply forgot.

workzap_build.text: reminders sent to customers for uncollected orders.

problems.ask_first: How much advance do you take?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, count uncollected finished orders hanging in the shop each evening, so you see how much cash is waiting on collection.
Keep one notebook of all ready but uncollected orders at the counter, so staff can follow up from one place.

problems.words: Customers keep calling to ask if clothes are ready
quick_ideas: Tell customers you'll message them when it's ready, so they stop calling
Keep a ready list at the counter, so anyone can answer.

workzap_build.text: "ready for collection" WhatsApp messages sent to customers.

problems.ask_first: How many orders do you deliver a day?
problems.free_stops: Message flow stays for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, note how many readiness calls come before noon and after noon, so you see when interruptions hit the counter hardest.
Give one person a fixed time to check which clothes are ready and update the counter list, so every caller gets the same answer quickly.

problems.words: Main shop and workshop don't know each other's status
quick_ideas: Share one daily list between shop and workshop, so both see the same status
Note orders sent and received, so nothing goes missing in between.
problems.ask_first: How far is the workshop from the shop?
problems.free_stops: Tracking setup is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, compare the shop's promised orders with the workshop's received bundles each evening, so missing handovers show the same day.
Set one fixed handover time for slips and fabric between shop and workshop, so both sides work from the same day's list.

problems.words: Cash in the drawer doesn't match the slips
quick_ideas: Count cash against slips at day end, so gaps show the same day
Record every advance and balance on the slip, so the drawer can be checked.
problems.free_stops: Reconciliation rules stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, note slip totals and drawer cash at closing on one page, so you see when mismatches usually start.
Make one person close the drawer and file all slips in one envelope each evening, so checking stops changing by shift.

never_say: Labour law, piece-rate legality or visa advice.
Storing a specific customer's measurements or photos through pi.
Help copying registered designs or counterfeits.
Workshop fire or electrical hazards mean emergency services first.

sample_reply.person: Eid se pehle bohat orders le liye, aadhe abhi cut bhi nahi hue. Kya karein?
sample_reply.pi:
Haan, is ko behtar kiya ja sakta hai, aur is ke liye bade kharch ki zaroorat nahi.
Pehle, pata kiya jaye ke team asal mein hafte mein kitne suit bana sakti hai.
Doosra, jab yeh had poori ho jaye to booking band kar di jaye.
Workzap ye sab ek jagah rakh sakta hai: booking ke waqt hi warning aaye jab orders capacity se barh jayein.
